title: Inverse-limit coefficient transport and scalar chain comparison
statement:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites and compatible small skeletons in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], and write $F=g^{-1}$ for inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheafified balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and cochain complexes with the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

For $W=X,Y$ let $(A_{W,m})_{m\geq1}$ and $(B_{W,m})_{m\geq1}$ be inverse systems of commutative ring sheaves with transitions $q^A_{W,m},q^B_{W,m}$ and compatible ring maps $i_{W,m}:A_{W,m}\to B_{W,m}$. Put $R_W=\varprojlim_m A_{W,m}$ and $S_W=\varprojlim_m B_{W,m}$, with projections $\pi^A_{W,m},\pi^B_{W,m}$ and induced map $j_W:R_W\to S_W$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Suppose given ring isomorphisms $c_{A,m}:FA_{Y,m}\simeq A_{X,m}$, $c_{B,m}:FB_{Y,m}\simeq B_{X,m}$ compatible with transitions and satisfying
$$c_{B,m}F(i_{Y,m})=i_{X,m}c_{A,m}.$$
Suppose given ring isomorphisms $c_R:FR_Y\simeq R_X$, $c_S:FS_Y\simeq S_X$ with
$$\pi^A_{X,m}c_R=c_{A,m}F(\pi^A_{Y,m}),\qquad \pi^B_{X,m}c_S=c_{B,m}F(\pi^B_{Y,m}).$$
Write $G_R,G_S$ for inverse image of modules or complexes with the scalar action transported along $c_R,c_S$, respectively. Then
$$c_SF(j_Y)=j_Xc_R.$$
For every, possibly unbounded, $R_Y$-module complex $P$ there is an $S_X$-linear isomorphism of complexes
$$b_P:G_RP\otimes_{R_X}S_X\xrightarrow{\sim}G_S(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y),$$
natural for all chain maps. It is characterized on local tensors by
$$b_P(Fp\otimes c_S(Fs_0))=F(p\otimes s_0).$$
Its inverse has the reverse displayed rule. Both maps commute with the differential $d_P\otimes1$ and carry chain homotopies to chain homotopies under the two termwise functors. No flatness or K-flatness is assumed.

proof.text: Use the normalized scalar-extension adjunctions. Transpose F(unit M) followed by the restriction square to construct a natural map F(M) extended along jX to G(M extended along jY). For targets G(N), composition with this map is the composite of the hom bijections for the two fully faithful transports, the two scalar adjunctions, and the restriction square. Essential surjectivity of G extends bijectivity to every target, so the map is invertible by the coyoneda criterion. The site and coefficient transports are equivalences by the existing site equivalence and Mathlib pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence.

proof.text: The adjunction unit equation evaluated at U gives the required comparison formula on 1 tensor p. Every s tensor p equals s acting on 1 tensor p, directly by linearity of the sheafification unit. Linearity of the comparison and cS inverse(cS(s))=s give the formula on cS(s) tensor p. Applying the inverse comparison gives its reverse formula. The scalar-extension adjunction also shows two maps equal if they agree on all 1 tensor p.

proof.text: Apply NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex to the module comparison, in every integer degree. Naturality supplies differential and chain-map compatibility. Naturality applied to each homotopy component gives both intertwining identities. For any other normalized natural isomorphism, compare its hom components degreewise using the preceding extension adjunction extensionality at scalar 1; then homological-complex, natural-transformation and isomorphism extensionality prove uniqueness.
